To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the peripheral blood immunome is dysregulated in familial and Hermansky-Pudadlak syndrome pulmonary fibroses; 2) the peripheral blood mononucleated cell gene expression profile is enriched for genes related to mitosis and cell cycling; 3) serum proteomic analyses reveal enrichment for cytokines, growth factors, and leptin; 4) peripheral blood immunome dysregulation is associated with pulmonary fibrosis severity

(1) the immunome in patients affected with familial pulmonary fibroses is characterized by increased proportion of activated central memory CD4 T cells, increased proportion and absolute number of B cells, and increased proportion of CD39+ T cells, whereas the proportion of CD39- CD4 T cells was reduced; (2) gene expression analysis of peripheral blood monocytes in patients affected with HPSPF revealed an enrichment of upregulated pathways involved in mitosis and cell-cycle control; (3)
we have shown that patients with pulmonary fibrosis have a unique blood immunome phenotype that may contribute to the pathogenesis of their disease.
